॥ Om, from the divine revelation of the place, etc. ॥ 1/2/14 ॥

The power of the place, as in “That which is poured as ghee or water upon the path goes along the path itself,” and the power of the Self, as in “Vamana” and “Bhamana,” are declared. For this is its sign. In the Chaturveda Shikha it is said: “He is the Lord, He is without a partner, He is Hari, He is the Supreme, the Highest of the high. That which is poured as ghee or water upon the path goes along the path itself. He is Vamana, He is Bhamana, He is Ananda, He is Achyuta.” And in the Vamana Upanishad: “That which, being the place, is this eye, unattached to all objects—He is Vamana, the Supreme, our goal; thus one should reflect.” ॥ 14 ॥
